context_documents.title: 2025-3663 · A sideways elevator makes pass-through feasible with different interference
context_documents.body:
# 2025-3663: A sideways elevator makes pass-through feasible with different interference

Focused study supplement. Not a full binder/CAD review, exhaustive subsystem specification, every-version history or visual interview watch.

## Published / retained construction account

The fourth arm/grabber iteration works beside a sideways-oriented elevator. The robot handles coral levels and algae with the same arm assembly. The interview also describes placing the battery to counter the elevator’s mass and moving the scoring arm clear during climbing.

## Team-stated reasoning or boundary

The team explicitly says it wanted pass-through behavior but did not consider passing through the elevator suitable for its resources. It identifies low center of gravity as a reason for the alternate arrangement.

## Engineering interpretation — analyst inference

Pass-through is a functional requirement, not a mandate to send the piece through an elevator opening. An offset mechanism can provide the desired acquisition/scoring directions while changing lateral load, frame torsion and the safe sweep envelope. Counterweight placement may improve static balance but should be checked throughout arm travel and with each game piece.

## Proposed validation — not performed

Measure lateral deflection and tip margin in the highest off-center pose; test all arm-to-climber transitions. Do not infer an undisclosed collector construction from the functional pass-through description.

## Limits

Focused technical passages and the retained dossier are the evidence scope. Exact event installation, complete CAD tolerances and all intermediate revisions are not certified.

## Sources and navigation

- [https://youtu.be/7lY_t0Ueh7U](https://youtu.be/7lY_t0Ueh7U)

source_reviews.title: 3663 CPR, Behind the Bumpers
source_reviews.locator: Clackamas interview, 1:19–2:25 design and software, 2:33–4:38 arm, 4:46–6:17 climb
source_reviews.review_basis: Read the on-page English transcript of team interview; no footage claims
facts: Team chose a sideways elevator with carriage-mounted arm for access around the elevator, moved wrist and grabber belts inside 2 by 2 aluminum by iteration four, and used an elevated-pivot cage latch that retained through gearing.
limitations: Captions describe demonstrations but do not establish exact roller geometry, rigging, physical speed or how long the cage retained load under worst-case conditions.

source_reviews.title: CPR team blog
facts: CPR reports demonstrating the 2025 machine with coral and algae, including scoring PVC coral on a reef at the Cedar Park Church Block Party.
limitations: Outreach copy gives capability context only and no hardware change log.

subsystems.name: Sideways lift and arm structure
subsystems.construction: Elevator presented sideways with a pivoting arm mounted on its carriage. The interview identifies 2 by 2 aluminum on the arm.
subsystems.operation: The lift supplies height and the arm reaches past the lift to move between intake and scoring presentations.
subsystems.team_rationale: The team wanted pass-through-style access and judged passing through the elevator itself unsuitable. They also aimed for a low center of gravity.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: If the carried arm and piece load the carriage off center, check guide loading and wrist deflection at reach. The benefit depends on access around the upright throughout the motion, including with a loaded tool.
subsystems.interfaces: Carriage reacts arm loads, and lift height sets the clearance available for pivoting near the bellypan.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: After impact, compare the measured tip path to its taught path before commanding an aggressive low transition.
subsystems.unknowns: Stage count, carriage guides, reduction, motor placement and exact motion limits.

subsystems.name: Wrist, grabber and scoring controls
subsystems.construction: Internal belts drive the wrist and grabber. The same tip handles coral and algae.
subsystems.operation: Present the tool for collection, keep the piece through the arm swing, then place it at the chosen target using the level-specific software pose and speed.
subsystems.team_rationale: External belts in early design were exposed to snagging on the reef. Software work emphasized avoiding robot and field collisions and placing pieces precisely.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Enclosing transmission reduces exposure to reef contact and can complicate belt inspection. A protective tube only helps if the service route permits restoring belt tension and wrist zero repeatably.
subsystems.interfaces: The 2 by 2 arm is both structure and transmission enclosure. Wrist orientation and chassis approach determine release geometry together.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Inspect belt tracking and exits after contact. Exercise collision limits with a real coral and algae, since each enlarges the moving envelope differently.
subsystems.unknowns: Internal reduction, grabber contact materials, sensing, calibration and release settings.

subsystems.name: Deep cage latch
subsystems.construction: Elevated pivot and latch that flips the cage; the final described holding method is drivetrain gearing within the climber, with a planned ratchet omitted.
subsystems.operation: Latch into the cage, rotate to move the suspended chain toward the robot middle and lower the scoring arm clear.
subsystems.team_rationale: Deep climb mattered for ranking points. CPR wanted a small package and designed around battery and elevator balance. The team reported gearing held long enough in its use.
subsystems.engineering_analysis: Measure the suspension point relative to the loaded center of mass. Small offsets change hanging angle and the loads on the latch and structure.
subsystems.interfaces: Climb rotation shares space with the arm. Battery location and mast mass influence hang attitude.
subsystems.service_and_failure_modes: Check gear backdrive after disable, with wear and the least favorable loading. Inspect cage pin and latch engagement after repeated off-center capture.
subsystems.unknowns: Gear reduction, latch actuation details and timed retention under varied loads.

source_review.whole_robot_explanation: Cedar Park made a lift with an arm mounted on the carriage. The sideways elevator layout let the arm reach around the lift to give the access pattern the team wanted from a pass-through robot. A common arm-tip grabber does coral and algae work. The arm changes position relative to the carriage, while the wrist sets the tool presentation. This arrangement puts the scoring routes and endgame into one shared clearance problem: the arm has to stay clear of the bellypan during ordinary motion and lower out of the climber's sweep during endgame.
source_review.piece_flow: The intake pose brings the carriage-mounted grabber to the piece. The common wrist and grabber take the piece through lift and arm motion, then the software selects the position and placement speed for the level. The team describes L1 through L4 coral and processor and net algae; in the interview they narrate a reef coral and a net algae demonstration. The exact floor versus station entry geometry, retention contacts and eject sequence remain unresolved.
source_review.packaging_and_motion: Separate the carriage's vertical travel, arm sweep, wrist motion and powered grabber from the pivoting cage system. The sideways elevator preserves arm access beside the mast, but the arm envelope includes the reef and the bellypan. A replacement belt, wrist zero or carriage repair should therefore be checked in transition as well as at the endpoints. The battery also serves as a packaging and balance constraint in the climb layout.
revisions: Team describes four arm and grabber design iterations, moving belts inward between the early and fourth designs. The ratchet remained a proposal in the described configuration.
transferable_principles: Translate the access objective into a tool path before selecting lift orientation. Protect belts where the tool enters field structure, and allocate a separate tested arm pose for the climber.
disconfirming_conditions: Mast-side reach loses value if carriage stiffness or arm clearance makes transitions slow. Gear-only cage holding needs reevaluation if load, lubrication or wear increases backdrive.
remaining_gaps: Exact acquisition method, lift rigging, swerve module specification, measured cycle and climb distributions, and later-event hardware chronology.
recommended_images: Interview arm chapter at 2:57–3:38 for a candidate side view of the carriage and internal-belt explanation.
Climb chapter at 5:27–5:53 for a candidate image of the cage pivot and arm clearance. Frame content still needs inspection.
